newsitem.title: USA: DuPont net up on oil products, chemicals.
newsitem.headline: DuPont net up on oil products, chemicals.

text.p: DuPont Co, reporting higher third quarter results, cited strong upstream petroleum earnings and 6.0 percent volume growth in its chemicals and specialties businesses.

Excluding a previously announced charge of $0.08 per share, earnings for the quarter were $1.68 a share, 22 percent higher than the $1.38 earned in the 1995 third quarter. Net income rose to $898 million from $769 million.
"This is the 10th consecutive quarter where earnings per share were at record levels versus comparable quarters," said Chief Executive Officer John Krol.

Petroleum segment earnings rose 47 percent from a year earlier and were the best since the 1991 first quarter, DuPont said. Upstream was particularly strong, with earnings up 96 percent on higher prices and solid production gains.

Earnings for Chemicals and Specialties businesses were mixed, with strong performances from agricultural products, automotive products, nylon, engineering polymers and LYCRA brand spandex, DuPont said.
Sales for the third quarter were $10.5 billion, versus $10.2 billion last year, up 3.0 percent, the company said.

Chemicals and Specialties segments sales were $5.6 billion, up 3.0 percent after adjusting for changes in business composition resulting from divestitures and formation of the DuPont Dow Elastomers joint venture.
Worldwide Chemicals and Specialties sales volume increased 6.0 percent -- 4.0 percent in the United States and 7.0 percent outside the United States.

DuPont said worldwide Chemicals and Specialties average selling prices were down 3.0 percent from a year earlier, about half of this due to the adverse effect of the stronger dollar and the remainder due primarily to lower prices for white pigments and DACRON polyester fiber.

Petroleum segment sales were $4.9 billion, up 12 percent. Crude oil prices averaged $19.85 per barrel, 25 percent higher than last year. U.S. natural gas prices were 45 percent higher, averaging $1.98 per thousand cubic feet, while worldwide gas prices increased 32 percent, to $2.28 per thousand cubic feet.
Crude oil production and natural gas deliveries increased 5.0 percent and 12 percent, respectively, DuPont said.
